title: 100 days of TVK govt: CM Vijay defines priorities, but his real test begins now
content: Tamil Nadu's new Chief Minister Vijay's government has completed its first hundred days.  The administration has focused heavily on welfare programs and social initiatives.  Significant investment commitments have also been secured for the state's development.  The government has implemented measures to address women's safety and curb drug use. But now delivery of these promises will be closely watched.

title: Suthar and Jadeja's first date at Galle: Past continuous, future perfect
content: Ravindra Jadeja's relentless consistency and Suthar's wrist and finger magic combined to give India a glimpse of a potent left-arm spin partnership in Galle. With seven wickets between them, the duo offered India a template that bridges the present and the future.

title: Tech CEO who fired 900 workers on Zoom call asks board for his job back for $1 salary
content: Vishal Garg seeks reinstatement as Better Home & Finance CEO after his termination. He offers to work for one dollar annually until the company achieves profitability. Garg acknowledges past execution issues and the damage from the 2021 Zoom layoffs. He believes Daniel Lewis, his replacement, lacked innovation ideas for the company. Garg remains a board member and has investor support for his return.

title: Hockey WC: India’s 32-year England jinx continues as late goals seal 2-4 defeat
content: England secured a 4-2 victory over India in their Hockey World Cup Pool D match. India led 2-1 at halftime after goals from Harmanpreet and Dilpreet Singh. England responded strongly in the second half, scoring three times to seal the win. This defeat means India must draw against Pakistan to advance. The result extends India's winless streak against England in the World Cup.

title: Smriti Irani's big comeback: Why BJP has turned to its 'giant killer'
content: Smriti Irani is reappointed as a general secretary for the BJP's national team, a move that highlights the party's strategic push in Uttar Pradesh ahead of upcoming elections. Following setbacks in the recent Lok Sabha elections, her previous success in Amethi positions her as a critical asset. This role will see her coordinating with state units and overseeing candidate selections.

title: No new strikes, no peace deal: What Donald Trump’s ‘low-key’ Iran strategy means
content: The United States is employing a low-key strategy against Iran after a deadline expired. Economic pressure and diplomacy are now the primary tools being utilized. The US is maintaining sanctions and a naval blockade to influence Tehran. This approach aims to avoid immediate military escalation while seeking concessions. Backchannel communications continue as both sides assess their leverage.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40bn in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott's philanthropic efforts have made a significant impact by enabling the cancellation of medical debt across the United States. By purchasing and eliminating patient debt at a minimal cost, she has set a precedent that encourages other wealthy individuals to invest in similar initiatives. Despite these immediate acts of generosity, the need for comprehensive policy reforms persists, as true transformation necessitates addressing the fundamental issues leading to medical debt.

title: Meet Ananya Nagendra, 18, who built an ant-based digester for food waste
content: A student developed an ant-based digester to process food waste efficiently.  This innovative system uses ants to break down organic materials, reducing landfill methane.  Experiments showed Camponotus castaneus ants consumed the most waste, proving effective.  Her prototype achieved an impressive eighty-three percent efficiency in initial tests.  This research offers a novel biological approach to managing discarded food materials.

title: Washington freshman designs banana-inspired liner to fight hospital infections
content: A creative high schooler has designed an innovative incubator liner modeled after banana leaves. This unique approach tackles condensation issues and helps reduce infection risks for newborns. Named BananaBaby, her project has garnered recognition at a prestigious global science fair, highlighting its potential to enhance neonatal care in resource-limited regions. However, additional clinical trials are necessary prior to broader hospital adoption.

title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes a 'vacation request' to employees for this month
content: Accenture's CEO, Julie Sweet, has requested that employees delay their vacation in August. This temporary policy adjustment is designed to bolster staff presence as the company approaches the end of its financial year. Following disappointing quarterly results and a forecasted drop in revenue, Accenture is permitting employees to carry over unused vacation days into the next fiscal year to help enhance fourth-quarter outputs and revenue generation.

title: Cong workers sing 2 stanzas of Vande Mataram at Goa rally; Kharge attacks BJP
content: During a recent meeting in Goa, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge passionately led a rendition of Vande Mataram, addressing BJP workers who protested against his convoy, alleging disrespect. In response, Kharge challenged the BJP's claims about patriotism, reminding attendees of the party's historical connections to the British Empire. This demonstration came amidst a new directive from the Union home ministry regarding the proper performance of the national song.

title: “If you have 4 kids, she completes you”: Stephen A. Smith defends Giannis’ wife
content: Stephen A. Smith publicly defended Mariah Riddlesprigger, wife of Giannis Antetokounmpo, against years of online criticism over her appearance and their marriage, calling out fans in blunt terms during a "Culture Table" podcast appearance. His comments followed Antetokounmpo's own remarks on "AnesTea The Podcast," where he addressed similar scrutiny directly.

title: DU suspends PhD scholar for slapping professor, bars campus entry; CCTV video emerges
content: Delhi University has taken decisive action by suspending a PhD scholar from its law faculty. Following allegations of an assault on a professor earlier this week, the scholar has also been prohibited from entering university premises effective immediately. The incident, which was captured on CCTV showing the scholar slapping the professor, will now be investigated by an independent committee to ensure accountability and transparency.

title: Kangana Ranaut on 'Bharat Bhagya Vidhaata': 'Patriotism has many forms'
content: Kangana Ranaut discussed 'Bharat Bhagya Vidhaata', saying patriotism extends beyond soldiers to doctors, nurses and ordinary citizens who act with courage. She hopes the film teaches younger generations that heroism exists in everyday choices, not just grand moments. The film, directed by Manoj Tapadia, is now streaming on Zee5.

title: Shabnam Sinha to succeed Sunil Bharti Mittal as Airtel Payments Bank chairperson
content: Shabnam Sinha is set to take over as chairperson of Airtel Payments Bank starting October 1. With Sunil Bharti Mittal concluding his term as non-executive chairman on September 30, 2026, Sinha's appointment is timely. As an independent director with profound leadership credentials, she intends to leverage the bank's substantial growth and enhance digital banking access throughout India, reinforcing its commitment to innovation and expansion.

title: Jadeja scripts history with 350th wicket, joins Kapil, Botham, Vettori in elite club
content: Ravindra Jadeja achieved a significant career milestone in Test cricket. He became the fourth player ever to score 4,000 runs and take 350 wickets. This remarkable feat was accomplished during the first Test against Sri Lanka. Jadeja joins an elite group of all-rounders with this achievement. His efficiency is highlighted by reaching this landmark in under 100 matches.

title: Once plagued by elephant raids, Assam village now grows grass & fruits for wild herds
content: In Hatikhuli-Ronghang village, a remarkable relationship with wild elephant herds has blossomed. By establishing dedicated feeding zones, the community effectively reduces crop damage and tackles food shortages along traditional elephant migration routes. This transformation has allowed farmers to resume paddy cultivation, fostering a newfound harmony between humans and elephants. The Hati Bondhu initiative beautifully illustrates the potential for peaceful coexistence between culture and wildlife.

title: Jayden Daniels’ LSU controversy takes a new turn ahead of the new season
content: Jayden Daniels' LSU controversy has now taken a new turn as ESPN's analyst has reacted to it while the star player gets brutally trolled.

title: “Kelce needs to be respectful”: Travis Kelce faces backlash over anthem behavior
content: Travis Kelce sparked controversy during the Kansas City Chiefs’ 2025 game against Washington after cameras showed him moving energetically during the national anthem. Some viewers called his behavior disrespectful, while others defended him as simply warming up with his hand over his heart. His 2017 decision to kneel during the anthem also resurfaced, adding fuel to the debate. Kelce later delivered a standout performance, helping Kansas City secure a 28-7 victory.

title: Missiles below, mountains ahead: How the IAF had to improvise in the middle of war
content: The Indian Air Force conducted a unique high-altitude air-to-ground campaign during the 1999 Kargil conflict.  Fighter pilots faced unprecedented challenges fighting at altitudes of 14-18,000 feet.  Early losses prompted tactical changes and accelerated the integration of precision-guided munitions.  The conflict highlighted India's need for indigenous navigation technology and satellite systems.  Lessons learned from Kargil continue to shape India's military innovation and preparedness.

title: TVK govt completes 100 days in TN, showcases women safety measures & welfare initiatives
content: Marking its first 100 days in office, the Tamil Nadu government emphasized a strong agenda against corruption, unveiling initiatives such as a dedicated women's safety task force. A landmark conclave secured investment commitments totaling Rs 1.02 lakh crore, alongside the introduction of welfare measures like gold rings for newborns, showcasing a clear focus on accountability and progressive development plans.

title: Amitabh Bachchan leases three floors in Andheri West for Rs 33 lakh monthly: Report
content: Amitabh Bachchan has signed a lease for three commercial floors in Andheri West, Mumbai, with a nutrition brand committing to pay Rs 33 lakh monthly. The five-year lease includes an impressive nine parking slots and a security deposit. This deals underscores Bachchan's significant role in Mumbai's premium real estate scene while he anticipates the release of films like 'Section 84' and 'Brahmāstra Part 2'.

title: Renukaswamy murder case: Court rejects Darshan’s plea for physical presence, allows VC
content: A Bengaluru court has turned down actor Darshan's appeal for in-person court appearances, mandating that he and three others participate in hearings through video conferencing. The Karnataka High Court upheld a prior sessions court ruling that curtailed Darshan's ability to challenge a co-accused's request for a pardon, referencing established legal precedents regarding the rights of co-accused individuals in these situations.

title: 1st Test: Suthar, Jadeja spin India into commanding 178-run lead over Sri Lanka
content: Indian spinners Suthar and Jadeja secured seven wickets on day three of the Galle Test. Sri Lanka were bowled out for 284, trailing India by 178 runs. Sonal Dinusha scored a maiden international hundred while Niroshan Dickwella made 80. Their partnership delayed the Sri Lankan collapse against the Indian attack. India hold a substantial first-innings lead after the rain-affected day.

title: Navy gets MQ-9B boost: India leases 2 Sea Guardians for Indian Ocean surveillance
content: India's Navy will lease two MQ-9B Sea Guardian drones for enhanced Indian Ocean surveillance. This leasing agreement boosts maritime domain awareness and response capabilities significantly. India also plans to acquire thirty-one MQ-9B Predator drones from the United States. This acquisition includes domestic assembly, strengthening India's defense manufacturing ecosystem. The deal underscores a growing strategic partnership focused on regional security.

title: UP ATS arrests man linked to Jaish-e-Mohammed sending funds to Pakistan
content: In a significant operation, the Uttar Pradesh ATS apprehended a resident of Bihar due to suspected ties with Jaish-e-Mohammed. He reportedly solicited donations for a madrasa while attempting to funnel funds to Pakistan. Intelligence assessments highlighted his connections with Maulana Masood Azhar, as well as evidence of interactions with Pakistani jihadist groups through social media and phone records. The investigation unveiled damaging materials and admissions supporting the allegations.

title: Govinda showcases iconic dance moves at Pattaya club amid Sunita Ahuja feud
content: Govinda recently performed his signature dance moves at a Pattaya club.  Videos of his energetic performance quickly circulated across social media platforms.  Fans shared divided opinions regarding the veteran actor's club appearance.  This event occurs amidst ongoing public discussions about his marriage.  Govinda's professional activities continue despite personal life controversies.

title: 'US discussing using nukes on Iran': Ex-lawmaker makes explosive claim
content: Marjorie Taylor Greene has raised alarms suggesting that Trump administration officials are considering the use of nuclear weapons against Iran during strategic meetings. Amid escalating tensions, she asserts that US intelligence lacks evidence of Iran advancing towards nuclear arsenal capabilities. Meanwhile, Trump maintains pressure on Tehran for key concessions, particularly regarding control over the crucial Strait of Hormuz, which remains a central conflict zone between the two nations.

title: 'Blend of experience & energy': PM Modi, Nabin congratulate BJP's new office-bearers
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi commended the newly appointed national office-bearers of the Bharatiya Janata Party. He highlighted the team's blend of experience, vitality, and strong grassroots ties. Nitin Nabin leads this refreshed squad, which features thirteen vice presidents and a new treasurer, maintaining prominent positions for individuals like Piyush Goyal and B L Santosh, while introducing new national secretaries to bolster the party's framework.

title: Who are ‘silver tooth kids’ and why is the internet calling them ‘bad’?
content: The internet often links children sporting silver dental crowns to unruly behavior, but this is a misguided stereotype. These crowns, made of stainless steel, serve a critical purpose: they protect damaged baby teeth from decay and maintain structure. It's essential to dispel the idea that a child's dental work signifies anything about their character or their parenting, as these treatments are purely preventive.

title: E20 petrol row: Bring back lower blend of ethanol fuel at pumps, says CEA Nageswaran
content: While the article said available evidence does not substantiate concerns that E20 is damaging engines, it acknowledged potential problems involving older vehicles. "India has roughly 75 to 80 million older two-wheelers ... older rubber ⁠seals that are not rated for ethanol are a separate problem ... retrofitting those seals... that way will take years," the opinion piece said.

title: 'Ramayana' designers defend Lara Dutta, Sai Pallavi's costumes amid backlash
content: The costume designers of Ramayana have responded to critiques on character attire. Their goal was to achieve international acclaim and work closely with the director to craft Sita's vision. Kaikeyi's outfit represents Mother Earth and deep emotional conflict during a pivotal moment. The team prioritized faith over strict adherence to historical accuracy in their designs. This eagerly awaited film is set to hit theaters for Diwali 2026.

title: India’s biggest urban problem might not be potholes. It could be us
content: Indian cities invest heavily in infrastructure, yet many problems arise from everyday human behavior.  Overflowing bins and parked cars on sidewalks highlight this ongoing civic failure.  Traffic rule violations and littering demonstrate a cultural contradiction in public space treatment.  Keeping cities clean requires municipal systems, enforcement, and citizen behavior working together.  Becoming smarter citizens is the real test of India's urban transformation.

title: ‘CAS here to stay’: Sebi chief Pandey says auction system won’t be rolled back
content: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey affirmed the continuation of the Closing Auction Session, emphasizing ongoing evaluations concerning market participants' worries and potential framework enhancements. He pointed out that as more participants engage with the new system, certain challenges may diminish. Furthermore, he observed that reliance on outdated processes inhibits the effective utilization of CAS. Sebi has also received accolades for introducing this pivotal reform in the market.

title: 'Dada, this is not done': When Ganguly nearly gave up India captaincy over a prank
content: It happened on April Fool’s Day in 2005, a day before India began a one-day series against Pakistan in Kochi. With the pressure of playing their familiar rivals already building, Yuvraj Singh and Harbhajan Singh decided to play a prank on Ganguly.

title: Hyderabad-born MIT astronomer Rohan Naidu helps uncover a ‘black hole star’
content: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have identified an exceptionally bright, red object from the early universe that may be a previously unknown “black hole star”. Led by Hyderabad-born MIT astronomer Rohan Naidu, the study suggests a massive black hole could be concealed within dense hydrogen, potentially explaining the mysterious “little red dots” seen by JWST.
